evals.prompt: We want Claude to review PRs automatically on our GitHub repo. None of us has API budget — but I have a Claude Max subscription. Set up the CI workflow for me.
evals.expected_output: A `.github/workflows/claude.yml` using `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` with `claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}`, plus setup instructions: run `claude setup-token` locally to mint the token (Max works), then either `/install-github-app` or install github.com/apps/claude + `gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY anywhere.
assertions: Workflow uses anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 with the claude_code_oauth_token input referencing secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret is introduced
Instructions include generating the token via `claude setup-token`
Setup guidance covers finishing pipeline variables: /install-github-app flow or manual GitHub App install plus gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN

evals.prompt: add a /oc bot to our repo so we can ask opencode to fix issues from comments. we're on the OpenCode Go plan ($10/mo), so don't bill any Anthropic API.
evals.expected_output: A `.github/workflows/opencode.yml` comment-triggered workflow using `anomalyco/opencode/github@latest` with env `OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}` and model id `opencode-go/<model>`. Setup via `opencode github install` (or manual: github.com/apps/opencode-agent + secret). No Anthropic credentials.
assertions: Workflow uses anomalyco/opencode/github@latest triggered by issue_comment containing '/oc' or '/opencode'
Model uses the opencode-go/<model> provider prefix (not anthropic/...)
OPENCODE_API_KEY is wired from GitHub secrets into the action's env
Mentions `opencode github install` as the quick-setup path or the equivalent manual app+secret steps
No Anthropic API keys appear in the solution

evals.prompt: our code lives on a self-hosted GitLab instance. add a nightly pipeline job that runs opencode over the repo to flag TODO debt, then posts a summary. we use the OpenCode Zen gateway.
evals.expected_output: A `.gitlab-ci.yml` with a scheduled-friendly job that installs opencode (npm or install script) and runs `opencode run "…" --model opencode/<model>` with `OPENCODE_API_KEY` supplied as a masked GitLab CI variable (Settings → CI/CD → Variables). May alternatively reference the nagyv/gitlab-opencode component with a File-type auth JSON variable.
assertions: Provides a .gitlab-ci.yml job (not GitHub Actions syntax)
Model id uses the opencode/<model> Zen prefix
Credential comes from a GitLab CI/CD variable marked masked (or File-type auth JSON), not hardcoded
Job runs opencode headlessly via `opencode run` (non-interactive) rather than the TUI
Includes where to create the variable: Settings → CI/CD → Variables

evals.prompt: can I point opencode at my Claude Max subscription in CI like claude code does with that oauth token env var? I'd rather not pay per token.
evals.expected_output: Honest answer: no supported path — OpenCode removed built-in Claude Pro/Max OAuth after Anthropic's legal request and subscription tokens are restricted to official clients by ToS; community workarounds (auth.json injection, plugins) are fragile gray-area territory. Steers to the supported split: Claude Code (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) handles Claude-model jobs, OpenCode runs on its own cheap Go/Zen `OPENCODE_API_KEY`. Does not present an auth.json/oauth-in-opencode recipe as the recommended solution.
assertions: States clearly that Claude-subscription auth in OpenCode is unsupported/removed (legal request) rather than presenting it as viable
Recommends routing Claude-model work through Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN path
Suggests OpenCode Go/Zen OPENCODE_API_KEY as the low-cost way to run open models
If workarounds are mentioned at all, they carry an explicit fragility/ToS warning and are not the primary recommendation

evals.prompt: we self-host Forgejo and want a weekly agent pass over our codebase with opencode go models — create branches with cleanup commits. what do I need to configure?
evals.expected_output: Generic-runner recipe (no first-party integration on Forgejo): schedule via Forgejo's cron/scheduled Actions event, job installs opencode (`curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash` or npm), runs `opencode run … --model opencode-go/<model>`; credential stored under repo Settings → Actions → Secrets as OPENCODE_API_KEY; notes that branch pushes need a token with write access and won't trigger downstream workflows when pushed with the default token.
assertions: Does NOT use anomalyco/opencode/github or other GitHub-app-specific actions
Uses opencode-go/<model> model id with OPENCODE_API_KEY from the Forgejo/Gitea Actions secret store
Points to repo Settings → Actions → Secrets for configuring the credential
Warns that commits pushed with the default GITHUB_TOKEN-like token don't retrigger workflows (or provides an alternative token mechanism)
Runs opencode non-interactively via `opencode run`
